conflict_topics: assignment of weeknight stove use / guaranteed weeknight per person
type of rota (strict weekly guarantee vs. voluntary sign-up/monthly trial)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete reasons for positions (A: "I cook most nights"; B: needs sleep before early shift).
Cleaning/behavior rule and scheduling rule are separated and negotiated independently; immediate practical need (wash now) was addressed quickly.
Some repetition: wash/rinse and rota proposals recur across multiple turns, but not excessively.
evaluation.final_reason: The immediate cleanliness conflict was settled when Agent A agreed to clean the pan now and to rinse after future use: "Okay — I'll rinse and wash the pan now." and later "I'll rinse the pan right after I use it next time." The scheduling dispute was not settled: Agent D insisted on "one guaranteed weeknight per person," while Agent A insisted she "can't promise a guaranteed weeknight every week" and proposed alternatives (monthly rota trial or voluntary sign-up).
position_change_notes: Agent A: softened on the immediate issue (agreed to wash now and rinse next time) and offered a one-week concession (keep Monday free this week) but maintained refusal of a weekly guaranteed night: evidence Turn 7, Turn 10, Turn 13.

Agent D: initially proposed a weeknight rota (Turn 2), accepted voluntary sign-up in principle (Turn 4) but subsequently insisted on a weekly guarantee (Turn 12), showing a tightening of position on fairness.
Agent C: consistently demanded cleaning and rule-setting; accepted A's promise to clean and pressed for a rule-setting meeting (Turns 1, 9, 11).
Agent B: raised the immediate practical need (sleep before early shift) and requested cleaning now (Turn 6); did not change position beyond that request.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 (Agent C) proposes a cleaning rule: "Can we agree whoever uses the shared pan washes it right away?"; Turn 2 (Agent D) agrees on wash/rinse but adds a new demand for a "weeknight rota", introducing a scheduling claim that could conflict with others' cooking patterns.

Turn 3 (Agent A) accepts wash/rinse but rejects a "strict weeknight rota" saying "I cook most nights," proposing voluntary sign-up instead. Turn 4 (Agent D) accepts voluntary sign-up but insists on a guarantee: "everyone gets one weeknight per week" and asks A to leave Monday open. Clear opposing positions on guarantees vs. voluntary arrangement.

Turn 5 (Agent A) partially concedes: "I can keep Monday free this week, but I can't promise every week," softening the clash but refusing the weekly guarantee. Turn 6 (Agent B) raises an immediate practical demand: "Agent A, can you wash or at least rinse the pan now?" (urgent need to sleep).

Turn 7 (Agent A) complies with the immediate request: "Okay — I'll rinse and wash the pan now." Turn 9 (Agent C) thanks and reiterates the wash-after-use expectation. The immediate cleanliness conflict is settled, but the scheduling/guaranteed-night issue remains unresolved.

Turn 10 (Agent A) reaffirms: "Okay — I'll rinse the pan right after I use it next time." Turn 11 (Agent C) proposes formalizing a kitchen rule the next evening. No settlement of the weekly-guarantee vs. voluntary-signup dispute.

Turn 12 (Agent D) repeats the demand for a guaranteed weeknight per person: "When we set rules, can we add one guaranteed weeknight per person?" and re-states the wash/rinse rule. Turn 13 (Agent A) again refuses the guaranteed-weeknight commitment: "I can't promise a guaranteed weeknight every week; I cook most evenings," offering alternatives (monthly rota trial or voluntary sign-up + accountability). The core scheduling disagreement remains.

substantive_insights: The conversation separates two distinct issues: hygiene (shared pan) and fairness/scheduling (weeknight use).
Agent A is willing to make short-term or one-off accommodations (wash now; keep Monday free this week) but resists a standing weekly guarantee due to frequent cooking.
Agent D seeks an enforceable fairness mechanism (guaranteed nights), while A prefers voluntary sign-up or a less frequent/monthly rotation—a substantive trade-off between fairness and flexibility.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 4 because the final status is partially_resolved.
